headline: All seven majors below the 200-day line; momentum shows fracture between assets; whales pulling Bitcoin off exchanges while funding diverges by venue.
paragraphs: The regime is bearish without exception. Bitcoin sits at 63,653.85, down 49% from its 12-month high of 124,773.51 and below the 200-day simple moving average. The same is true across all six other tracked assets: Ethereum at 1,904.72 (60.6% below peak), Solana at 73.25 (70.4% down), XRP at 1.07 (67.7% down), BNB at 570.53 (56.4% down), Dogecoin at 0.0704 (75.7% down), and Cardano at 0.1621 (83.2% down). None have registered a golden cross, and only two assets, BNB and Dogecoin, show MACD above signal line. The 50/200 cross is dormant across the board. Extreme Fear registers at 25 on the fear-greed scale, within a tight 30-day range of 20 to 33, suggesting the crowd has been terrified and remains terrified. This is a market where every major asset is in a defined downtrend against the long-term average.

Momentum, however, reveals tension. Bitcoin's RSI-14 sits at 47.4, neutral and neither oversold nor overbought, while MACD remains below signal. This suggests Bitcoin is drifting rather than collapsing; the selling pressure has not accelerated. Ethereum presents a different picture: RSI of 56.3 (above the 50 midpoint) paired with negative MACD, which is a mild divergence, momentum readings suggest relative strength but the trend indicator says momentum is waning. Solana and XRP are both oversold (RSI 42.7 and 42.9 respectively), yet both continue to trade below the 200-day line with MACD still below signal, meaning the oversold condition has not yet translated into a trend reversal. BNB and Dogecoin stand alone with MACD above signal, but neither is above the 200-day moving average and both trade well below their 12-month highs. The cross-asset pattern is fragmented: most assets are nearing or at oversold extremes, but the trend-following indicators are not backing up a bounce.

Derivative positioning shows a market where leverage is concentrated in longs and pricing has become uneven. Bitcoin's funding rate is essentially flat at 0.02% annualized, and open interest stands at 1.99 billion USD with a long-to-short ratio of 1.35, meaningful but not extreme. Ethereum tells a sharper story: funding is negative at minus 5.5% annualized, a signal that shorts are being paid to hold positions, yet open interest is 1.34 billion USD and the long-to-short ratio has swollen to 1.74. This mismatch (crowded longs, shrinking funding cost for shorts) suggests the leverage structure is unstable. In smaller-cap names, the positioning becomes lopsided. Solana's ratio is 2.55 longs per short, XRP's is 3.09, and Dogecoin reaches 4.87 longs per short, with funding rates at Solana (9.4% annualized), XRP (6.9%), and Dogecoin (6.2%) indicating that longs are paying to hold. Over the last 24 hours, short liquidations have dominated the tape: Bitcoin saw 4.23 million USD in shorts liquidated against only 1.09 million in longs; Ethereum saw 5.15 million in shorts liquidated against 2.71 million in longs; Solana had 497,000 in shorts liquidated versus 94,000 in longs. This pattern, lopsided long ratios, high long funding fees in smaller assets, and relentless short liquidations, describes a market where longs are crowded and expensive.

Whale and stablecoin flows show a bifurcated signal. Over the last 24 hours, 185.9 million USD of Bitcoin moved off exchanges (net outflow), with 114.3 million and 71.5 million leaving Kraken specifically. This is the kind of cold-storage move that often accompanies a lack of seller urgency: entities are removing coins from venues where they could be sold quickly, which contradicts panic. At the same time, stablecoin inflows are mixed: 119.9 million USD in USDC moved onto Coinbase Institutional and 102.8 million in USDT moved onto Bitfinex, yet 174.8 million in USDT moved off OKEx. Net stablecoin float has declined 0.86% over the last 30 days to 305.8 billion USD, a slow drain of dry powder. The weekly whale flow trend over the last four weeks shows extreme swings: minus 135 million, minus 131.5 million, then plus 835 million, then plus 1.2 billion. The two most recent weeks were heavy inflows, but today's single-day Bitcoin outflow suggests the momentum may be reversing; only one session of same-direction data is insufficient to call a new trend, but the tension between cold-storage removal and limited stablecoin cash accumulation is notable.

On-chain spot ETF flows provide a final layer. Bitcoin ETFs recorded a net inflow of 170.1 million USD on August 3rd, with a five-session rolling total of 120.2 million. Ethereum ETFs, by contrast, posted minus 11.9 million on the same day and minus 13.6 million over five sessions. Only one day of positive direction is printed for both, so persistence is not confirmed. Cumulative flows remain deeply positive (Bitcoin at 51.5 billion, Ethereum at 11.2 billion), but recent action shows Bitcoin receiving institutional bid while Ethereum is drifting lower. Market cap rose 0.62% in the last 24 hours to 2.28 trillion USD, a minor move. Bitcoin dominance holds steady at 56.6%.

Watch for three conditions: first, whether Bitcoin's RSI and MACD confirm a bounce attempt by moving above 50 and crossover respectively while price reclaims the 200-day line (currently around 65,500 estimated), a technical reset that would alter regime; second, whether Ethereum's negative funding stabilizes or turns positive, signaling either a short squeeze or renewed long conviction; and third, whether next week's whale flows return to the minus pattern (off-exchange moves continuing to accelerate) or swing back into stablecoin accumulation and exchange inflows, the latter of which would suggest preparation for selling. The tape today is a market treading water under extreme fear, longs crowded and paying to hold, but whales showing no panic to unload.
